Subject: Pilot with preview model - temporary uptime/latency commitments?

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our platform team ran an initial soak with the preview model (redwood-text-preview-v2) and we saw promising results for intent classification, but we also hit a number of latency spikes during peak auth windows. For our payments use case, predictable latency is critical during peak weekend traffic.

We want to move ahead with a controlled pilot (100k requests/day) next month, but procurement requires explicit SLOs. We understand this is a preview model — would Redwood consider a temporary, timeboxed adjustment to the uptime/latency SLOs for the pilot period with compensating controls (e.g., automatic fallback to a stable model, enhanced monitoring, and credits if the pilot causes production-visible failures)?

Specific asks:
- Temporary SLO: reduce availability commitment to a pilot-safe level (we would propose 99.0% for the pilot window), and relax p95 latency to 350ms for the preview model only.
- Clear rollback and fallback behavior if error or latency regressions appear.
- A credit mechanism if incidents affect our production customers.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will consider a formal carveout for a limited pilot and what controls you'd need from Greenfield to approve?

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director, Platform Engineering
Greenfield Payments

Hi all,

Draft proposal below — focused on minimizing customer impact while protecting Redwood's production guarantees. Suggest we present this as a limited "Pilot Exception Agreement" (PEA). Key points: 

1) Scope and duration
- Preview model: redwood-text-preview-v2 (pilot traffic pin to preview model endpoints)
- Pilot window: 2026-04-15 to 2026-05-15 (30 days)
- Traffic cap: 100k requests/day, and Redwood will rate-limit beyond that to enforce the pilot scope.

2) SLO adjustments (pilot-only)
- Availability SLO: temporarily set to 99.0% measured at the endpoint level for preview model traffic.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 350ms for preview model calls. Stable models continue to carry standard SLOs (99.9% / p95 <= 120ms).

3) Operational controls and monitoring
- Greenfield will provide a read-only Prometheus endpoint or API token for request/latency metrics and will enable request-level tracing headers so Redwood can correlate traces.
- Redwood will enable an elevated monitoring dashboard (pilot cluster) with 1-minute alerting during the pilot window and daily summary reports.

4) Fallbacks and rollback triggers
- Automatic fallback: On sustained p95 latency > 600ms for 10 consecutive minutes OR error rate > 2% for 5 minutes, traffic will be automatically routed to the pinned stable model.
- Manual rollback: either party can request immediate rollback with 2-hour SLA for execution (operational runbook attached).

5) Credits and liability
- If the preview endpoint causes production-impacting incidents for Greenfield customers, Redwood will issue a pilot credit equal to 25% of that pilot month's usage fees (applied to next invoice), capped at $50k.
- The pilot exception is explicit: Redwood's standard SLA remains in place for stable models; the PEA only modifies commitments for the preview model and only for the pilot window.

6) Termination and extension
- Either party can terminate the pilot with 48 hours' notice. Any extension requires written consent and mutual agreement on updated SLOs.

I've attached a short runbook and a one-page PEA draft. Legal should review the credit/cap wording. Karthik, can you confirm the automatic fallback mechanism and that routing to stable models will be seamless for customer traffic (no token re-issuance required)?

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Mina / Elena,

Confirming technical feasibility and a few clarifications:

- Automatic fallback: supported. We can route the incoming request IDs to the stable model instance transparently using the routing header (x-redwood-preferred-model). No client-side changes required.
- Rollback SLA: 2 hours is realistic for the standard runbook if we have the elevated monitoring and the sampling traces enabled up front.
- Observability: We recommend adding a 10% sampling of full traces during the first 72 hours of the pilot to speed diagnosis; this will be scoped to the pilot traffic only.
- Performance bands: the 350ms p95 is achievable under expected load with the preview model if we enable KV-cache warmup and continuous batching on the pilot pool. We will provision an autoscaling buffer for weekend peaks (configurable).

Minor ask for Greenfield: please provide a list of three high-volume endpoints (auth, charge-init, settlement-lookup) so we can create targeted synthetic tests during the pilot.

Happy to walk through runbook with your SREs.

Karthik
